newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares gain as focus settles on banks.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares gain as focus settles on banks.

text.p: Norwegian shares gained across the board on Friday on a firmer Wall Street and slightly lower interest rates, but dealers said the outlook remained uncertain due to concerns over the dollar and interest rates.

All sectors ended in positive territory before the weekend break and the Total share index advanced 0.82 percent to close at 1,064.18 points. Turnover, buoyed by heavy trade in the banking sector, amounted to 1.55 billion crowns.
The top two traded shares were Fokus Bank and Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbank), which together accounted for 472 million crowns of business.

Fokus, bidding to takeover BNbank, was forced to upgrade its exchange ratio offer to 3.4 Fokus shares for each share in BNbank after Norway's largest commercial bank Den norske Bank (DnB) made a counterbid for the niche mortgage lender.
BNbank shares surged on Fokus' renewed bid and closed 6.50 percent up at 206 crowns. Fokus, which was trading four crowns ex-dividend, ended unchanged at 59 crowns.
DnB, which made a cash offer of 184.50 crowns per share, plus BNbank's 1996 dividend of 10.50 crowns to value BNbank at NOK 1.902 billion crowns, finished the session 0.90 crowns higher at 28 crowns.
